- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Unfused `TEGroupedMLP` can create large FP32 temporaries when it weights low-precision activations with FP32 router probabilities.

This change chunks large products and recomputes supported, parameter-free GLU activations during backward while preserving activation rounding and the forward CUDA autocast context.

:warning: For major changes (either in lines of code or in its impact), please make sure to first share a design doc with the team. If you're unsure what's the best way to do so, contact NVIDIA/mcore-oncall.

## Issue tracking

For PRs from open-source community contributors:

- **New features**: a linked issue is **required**. Please open a [feature request](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/new?template=feature_request.md) and reference it here before submitting the PR.
- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Linked issue: None. This fixes a reproduced allocation problem.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR

### Code review

Feel free to message or comment NVIDIA/mcore-oncall to help accelerate your merge into main. The less complex your PR is, the faster it will be approved and merged!

All PRs start as **draft**. If you open a non-draft PR, it will be automatically converted to draft.

#### Step 1: Mark PR as "Ready for Review"

1. When your PR is ready, click **Ready for Review**.
2. An oncall reviewer is auto-assigned and expert reviewers are notified based on your changes.
   - Some PRs may jump straight to step 2. This is determined by `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

:warning: Only mark as ready once merge-conflicts are resolved and the CI is passing.
Final Review might get declined if these requirements are not fulfilled.

#### Step 2: Final Review

For PRs that change `megatron/core`, once all expert reviewers have approved, the `Final Review` label is applied **automatically** and final reviewers are assigned.

For PRs outside `megatron/core`, this step is skipped.

#### Step 3: Approved

Once all required reviewers have approved, the `Approved` label is applied **automatically**.

### Merge

Any member of [mcore-engineers](https://github.com/orgs/NVIDIA/teams/mcore-engineers) will be able to merge your PR.


## Testing

Targeted CUDA correctness, autocast backward, activation checkpointing, and determinism replay passed on the pinned NGC base with its bundled Transformer Engine. Formatting, lint, and the determinism coverage gate passed; optional mypy was unavailable.

Broader MoE tests hit backend limitations that also reproduce on the base revision with this GPU/TE setup. Full CI-image and multi-GPU validation still need maintainer CI vetting and the `Run functional tests` label.

The standard unit-test entry point in the CI container is:

```sh
uv run python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc-per-node=8 -m pytest tests/unit_tests
```

See the [testing guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/skills/mcore-testing/SKILL.md) for setup and focused runs.

### Downsides

The chunked path supports first-order gradients only and adds Python chunk iteration and activation recomputation. CUDA router gradients can differ from the native expression by FP32 reduction roundoff; repeated chunked executions remain bit-exact.

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Mixture-of-experts operations with per-token router probabilities.
+
+Router weighting consumes activations shaped ``[tokens, features]`` and
+probabilities shaped ``[tokens, 1]``, returning the activation dtype. The eager
+path also accepts other broadcastable layouts. Weighted GLU operations consume
+FC1 outputs and return the row-local activation's feature width.
+
+These operations own no parameters or persistent state and perform no
+communication. Callers supply tensors that are already local to an expert rank.
+"""

@@ -0,0 +1,162 @@
+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Bound mixed-precision router weighting in the forward and backward passes."""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import torch
+from torch.autograd.function import once_differentiable
+
+_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS = 16 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+class _ChunkedRouterWeight(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Multiply router probabilities without retaining a full promoted product."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, activations, probs, chunk_rows):
+        """Apply the original promoted product to bounded row chunks."""
+        ctx.save_for_backward(activations if ctx.needs_input_grad[1] else None, probs)
+        ctx.activation_dtype = activations.dtype
+        ctx.chunk_rows = chunk_rows
+        ctx.product_dtype = torch.promote_types(activations.dtype, probs.dtype)
+        output = torch.empty_like(activations)
+        for start in range(0, activations.shape[0], chunk_rows):
+            end = start + chunk_rows
+            output[start:end].copy_(
+                (activations[start:end] * probs[start:end]).to(activations.dtype)
+            )
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        """Return activation and router gradients without a full promoted product."""
+        activations, probs = ctx.saved_tensors
+        grad_activations = torch.empty_like(grad_output) if ctx.needs_input_grad[0] else None
+        grad_probs = torch.empty_like(probs) if ctx.needs_input_grad[1] else None
+        for start in range(0, grad_output.shape[0], ctx.chunk_rows):
+            end = start + ctx.chunk_rows
+            # Match the gradient of the cast after the original promoted product.
+            grad = grad_output[start:end].to(ctx.product_dtype)
+            if grad_activations is not None:
+                grad_activations[start:end].copy_(
+                    (grad * probs[start:end]).to(ctx.activation_dtype)
+                )
+            if grad_probs is not None:
+                grad_probs[start:end].copy_(
+                    (grad * activations[start:end]).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).to(probs.dtype)
+                )
+        return grad_activations, grad_probs, None
+
+
+class _ChunkedWeightedActivation(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Recompute a pointwise activation one row chunk at a time during backward."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @torch.amp.custom_fwd(device_type="cuda")
+    def forward(ctx, activation_func, inputs, probs, chunk_rows):
+        """Save inputs instead of retaining full eager activation intermediates."""
+        ctx.save_for_backward(inputs, probs)
+        ctx.activation_func = activation_func
+        ctx.chunk_rows = chunk_rows
+        output = None
+        for start in range(0, inputs.shape[0], chunk_rows):
+            end = start + chunk_rows
+            activation = activation_func(inputs[start:end])
+            if output is None:
+                output = activation.new_empty((inputs.shape[0], activation.shape[1]))
+            output[start:end].copy_((activation * probs[start:end]).to(activation.dtype))
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @torch.amp.custom_bwd(device_type="cuda")
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        """Recompute each activation chunk with its forward autocast context."""
+        inputs, probs = ctx.saved_tensors
+        needs_input, needs_probs = ctx.needs_input_grad[1:3]
+        grad_inputs = torch.empty_like(inputs) if needs_input else None
+        grad_probs = torch.empty_like(probs) if needs_probs else None
+        for start in range(0, inputs.shape[0], ctx.chunk_rows):
+            end = start + ctx.chunk_rows
+            with torch.enable_grad():
+                local_input = inputs[start:end].detach().requires_grad_(needs_input)
+                local_probs = probs[start:end].detach().requires_grad_(needs_probs)
+                activation = ctx.activation_func(local_input)
+                weighted = (activation * local_probs).to(activation.dtype)
+                variables = [value for value in (local_input, local_probs) if value.requires_grad]
+                gradients = iter(torch.autograd.grad(weighted, variables, grad_output[start:end]))
+            if grad_inputs is not None:
+                grad_inputs[start:end].copy_(next(gradients))
+            if grad_probs is not None:
+                grad_probs[start:end].copy_(next(gradients))
+        return None, grad_inputs, grad_probs, None
+
+
+def apply_weighted_activation(
+    activation_func: Callable[[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
+    inputs: torch.Tensor,
+    probs: torch.Tensor,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Recompute large mixed-precision activations for first-order training.
+
+    Save FC1 inputs and probabilities instead of full eager GLU intermediates.
+    Use the original activation and autograd in each chunk to retain its dtype
+    rounding, clamp derivatives, and router probability gradients.
+    The callback must be deterministic, pointwise, and parameter-free.
+
+    Args:
+        activation_func: A deterministic, parameter-free, row-local activation.
+        inputs: FC1 outputs with shape ``[tokens, features]``.
+        probs: Router probabilities with shape ``[tokens, 1]``.
+
+    Returns:
+        Router-weighted activations in the activation's original dtype.
+
+    Note:
+        The chunked path supports first-order gradients only. Small inputs and
+        inputs without dtype promotion keep the original autograd path.
+        CUDA router gradients can differ by FP32 reduction roundoff.
+    """
+    if (
+        inputs.numel() <= _MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS
+        or torch.promote_types(inputs.dtype, probs.dtype) == inputs.dtype
+        or inputs.ndim != 2
+        or probs.shape != (inputs.shape[0], 1)
+    ):
+        activation = activation_func(inputs)
+        return apply_router_probs(activation, probs)
+    chunk_rows = max(1, _MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS // inputs.shape[1])
+    return _ChunkedWeightedActivation.apply(activation_func, inputs, probs, chunk_rows)
+
+
+def apply_router_probs(activations: torch.Tensor, probs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Keep FP32 router weights without a full-size promoted activation tensor.
+
+    Large dropless expert batches can receive far more tokens than a balanced
+    rank. Target chunks of at most 16M elements, or 64 MiB for FP32, with a
+    minimum of one row per chunk. A wider row exceeds that target.
+    The output, saved activations, and returned gradients retain their original
+    precision. Small batches and products without dtype promotion use autograd.
+
+    Args:
+        activations: Expert activations with shape ``[tokens, features]``.
+        probs: Router probabilities broadcastable to the activations.
+
+    Returns:
+        The weighted activation in its original dtype.
+
+    Note:
+        The chunked path supports first-order gradients only. Other layouts keep
+        native broadcasting and autograd.
+        CUDA router gradients can differ by FP32 reduction roundoff.
+    """
+    if (
+        activations.numel() <= _MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS
+        or torch.promote_types(activations.dtype, probs.dtype) == activations.dtype
+        or activations.ndim != 2
+        or probs.shape != (activations.shape[0], 1)
+    ):
+        return (activations * probs).to(activations.dtype)
+    chunk_rows = max(1, _MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS // activations.shape[1])
+    return _ChunkedRouterWeight.apply(activations, probs, chunk_rows)

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+
+"""Replay chunked router weighting under concurrent GPU work."""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+from megatron.core.activations import squared_relu
+from megatron.core.ops.moe import weighted_activation
+from tests.unit_tests.determinism.kernels.harness import assert_replays_bit_exact, seeded
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("activation", [None, F.silu, squared_relu])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_chunked_weighting_replays_bit_exact(monkeypatch, activation, dtype):
+    """Replay outputs and both input gradients across full and partial chunks."""
+    seeded()
+    monkeypatch.setattr(weighted_activation, "_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS", 256 * 1024)
+    features = 4096
+    inputs = torch.randn(
+        513, features * (2 if activation else 1), device="cuda", dtype=dtype, requires_grad=True
+    )
+    probs = torch.rand(513, 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+
+    def glu(values):
+        gate, linear = values.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+        return activation(gate) * linear
+
+    def apply(values, weights):
+        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=dtype, enabled=activation is squared_relu):
+            if activation is not None:
+                return weighted_activation.apply_weighted_activation(glu, values, weights)
+            return weighted_activation.apply_router_probs(values, weights)
+
+    assert_replays_bit_exact(
+        apply, (inputs, probs), replays=3, contention=True, what="chunked router weighting"
+    )

+# Copyright (c) 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.
+"""Check router-weighted activations and their mixed-precision memory bound."""
+
+import os
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from torch.utils._python_dispatch import TorchDispatchMode
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def implementation(monkeypatch):
+    """Exercise chunk boundaries with small tensors without changing the public API."""
+    from megatron.core.ops.moe import weighted_activation
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(weighted_activation, "_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS", 32)
+    return vars(weighted_activation)
+
+
+def _reference(activations: torch.Tensor, probs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return (activations * probs).to(activations.dtype)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("requires_grad", [(True, True), (True, False), (False, True)])
+def test_outputs_and_gradients_match(
+    implementation: dict[str, Any], dtype: torch.dtype, requires_grad: tuple[bool, bool]
+) -> None:
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(421)
+    values = torch.randn(13, 7, generator=generator, dtype=dtype)
+    weights = torch.rand(13, 1, generator=generator, dtype=torch.float32)
+    upstream = torch.randn(values.shape, generator=generator, dtype=dtype)
+
+    def evaluate(function: Callable[..., torch.Tensor]) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        activations = values.clone().requires_grad_(requires_grad[0])
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_(requires_grad[1])
+        output = function(activations, probs)
+        inputs = [tensor for tensor in (activations, probs) if tensor.requires_grad]
+        return output, *torch.autograd.grad(output, inputs, upstream)
+
+    actual = evaluate(implementation["apply_router_probs"])
+    expected = evaluate(_reference)
+    for left, right in zip(actual, expected, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(left, right, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+class _LargeFloatIntermediates(TorchDispatchMode):
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.largest = 0
+
+    def __torch_dispatch__(self, func, types, args=(), kwargs=None):
+        output = func(*args, **(kwargs or {}))
+        if (
+            isinstance(output, torch.Tensor)
+            and output.dtype == torch.float32
+            and output.ndim == 2
+            and output.shape[-1] > 1
+        ):
+            self.largest = max(self.largest, output.numel())
+        return output
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("phase", ["forward", "backward"])
+def test_promoted_intermediates_are_bounded(implementation: dict[str, Any], phase: str) -> None:
+    activations = torch.randn(31, 7, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(31, 1, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+    apply = implementation["apply_router_probs"]
+    products = _LargeFloatIntermediates()
+    if phase == "forward":
+        with products:
+            output = apply(activations, probs)
+    else:
+        output = apply(activations, probs)
+        with products:
+            torch.autograd.grad(output, (activations, probs), torch.ones_like(output))
+    assert output.shape == activations.shape
+    assert 0 < products.largest <= implementation["_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS"]
+
+
+def test_existing_expression_exceeds_bound(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """The failed expression creates a full FP32 product before the BF16 cast."""
+    activations = torch.randn(31, 7, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    probs = torch.rand(31, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+    products = _LargeFloatIntermediates()
+    with products:
+        _reference(activations, probs)
+    assert products.largest > implementation["_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS"]
+
+
+def test_constant_router_weights_do_not_retain_activations(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    activations = torch.randn(31, 7, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(31, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+    saved_bytes = 0
+
+    def pack(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        nonlocal saved_bytes
+        saved_bytes += tensor.untyped_storage().nbytes()
+        return tensor
+
+    with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack, lambda tensor: tensor):
+        output = implementation["apply_router_probs"](activations, probs)
+    assert output.requires_grad
+    assert saved_bytes <= probs.untyped_storage().nbytes()
+    expected = _reference(activations, probs)
+    actual_grad = torch.autograd.grad(output, activations, torch.ones_like(output))[0]
+    expected_grad = torch.autograd.grad(expected, activations, torch.ones_like(expected))[0]
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_grad, expected_grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [0, 1, 4, 5, 13])
+def test_empty_and_chunk_boundary_sizes(implementation: dict[str, Any], rows: int) -> None:
+    activations = torch.randn(rows, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(rows, 1, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+    output = implementation["apply_router_probs"](activations, probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(output, _reference(activations, probs), rtol=0, atol=0)
+    gradients = torch.autograd.grad(output, (activations, probs), torch.ones_like(output))
+    assert gradients[0].shape == activations.shape
+    assert gradients[1].shape == probs.shape
+
+
+def test_recomputed_activation_matches(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint
+
+    values = torch.randn(13, 14, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = torch.rand(13, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    def evaluate(function: Callable[..., torch.Tensor]) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        inputs = values.clone().requires_grad_()
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_()
+
+        def layer(inputs, probs):
+            gate, linear = inputs.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+            activation = torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * linear
+            return function(activation, probs)
+
+        output = checkpoint(layer, inputs, probs, use_reentrant=True)
+        output.sum().backward()
+        assert inputs.grad is not None
+        assert probs.grad is not None
+        return output, inputs.grad, probs.grad
+
+    for actual, expected in zip(
+        evaluate(implementation["apply_router_probs"]), evaluate(_reference), strict=True
+    ):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_noncontiguous_activations_and_no_grad(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    activations = torch.randn(7, 13, dtype=torch.bfloat16).t()
+    probs = torch.rand(13, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        actual = implementation["apply_router_probs"](activations, probs)
+        expected = _reference(activations, probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_native_broadcasting_is_preserved(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    activations = torch.randn(13, 7, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    probs = torch.rand(7, dtype=torch.float32)
+    actual = implementation["apply_router_probs"](activations, probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, _reference(activations, probs), rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def _glu(inputs: torch.Tensor, clamp: float | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
+    gate, linear = inputs.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    if clamp is not None:
+        gate = gate.clamp(max=clamp)
+        linear = linear.clamp(min=-clamp, max=clamp)
+    return torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * (linear + 0.2)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("enabled", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_recomputed_activation_preserves_autocast(
+    implementation: dict[str, Any], enabled: bool, dtype: torch.dtype
+) -> None:
+    """Backward must reuse forward precision after its autocast scope has ended."""
+    from megatron.core.activations import squared_relu
+
+    device = torch.device("cuda", int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", "0")))
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(421)
+    values = torch.randn(13, 14, device=device, dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
+    weights = torch.rand(13, 1, device=device, dtype=torch.float32, generator=generator)
+    upstream = torch.randn(13, 7, device=device, dtype=torch.float32, generator=generator)
+
+    def activation(inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        gate, linear = inputs.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+        return squared_relu(gate) * linear
+
+    def evaluate(chunked: bool) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        inputs = values.clone().requires_grad_()
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_()
+        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=dtype, enabled=enabled):
+            if chunked:
+                output = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](activation, inputs, probs)
+            else:
+                output = _reference(activation(inputs), probs)
+        # Change the chunked backward's ambient state; keep native backward outside AMP.
+        with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=dtype, enabled=not enabled if chunked else False):
+            gradients = torch.autograd.grad(output, (inputs, probs), upstream.to(output.dtype))
+        return output, *gradients
+
+    for actual, expected in zip(evaluate(True), evaluate(False), strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="requires CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("gated", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+def test_cuda_partial_chunk_matches_native(monkeypatch, gated: bool, dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    """Compare CUDA outputs and gradients with a one-row tail chunk."""
+    from megatron.core.ops.moe import weighted_activation
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(weighted_activation, "_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS", 256 * 1024)
+    device = torch.device("cuda", int(os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", "0")))
+    generator = torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(421)
+    rows, features = 129, 4096
+    values = torch.randn(
+        rows, features * (2 if gated else 1), device=device, dtype=dtype, generator=generator
+    )
+    weights = torch.rand(rows, 1, device=device, dtype=torch.float32, generator=generator)
+    upstream = torch.randn(rows, features, device=device, dtype=dtype, generator=generator)
+
+    def activation(inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return _glu(inputs, clamp=0.75)
+
+    def evaluate(chunked: bool) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        inputs = values.clone().requires_grad_()
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_()
+        if gated and chunked:
+            output = weighted_activation.apply_weighted_activation(activation, inputs, probs)
+        elif chunked:
+            output = weighted_activation.apply_router_probs(inputs, probs)
+        else:
+            output = _reference(activation(inputs) if gated else inputs, probs)
+        return output, *torch.autograd.grad(output, (inputs, probs), upstream)
+
+    actual_output, actual_inputs, actual_probs = evaluate(True)
+    expected_output, expected_inputs, expected_probs = evaluate(False)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_output, expected_output, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_inputs, expected_inputs, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    # CUDA reductions can use a different FP32 summation tree for the tail row.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_probs, expected_probs)
+    activations = activation(values) if gated else values
+    precise_probs = (
+        (upstream.float() * activations).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True, dtype=torch.float64).float()
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual_probs, precise_probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(expected_probs, precise_probs)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("requires_grad", [(True, True), (True, False), (False, True)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("clamp", [None, 0.75])
+def test_weighted_glu_outputs_and_gradients_match(
+    implementation: dict[str, Any],
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    requires_grad: tuple[bool, bool],
+    clamp: float | None,
+) -> None:
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(512)
+    values = torch.randn(13, 14, generator=generator, dtype=dtype)
+    weights = torch.rand(13, 1, generator=generator, dtype=torch.float32)
+    upstream = torch.randn(13, 7, generator=generator, dtype=dtype)
+
+    def activation(inputs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return _glu(inputs, clamp)
+
+    def evaluate(chunked: bool) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        inputs = values.clone().requires_grad_(requires_grad[0])
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_(requires_grad[1])
+        if chunked:
+            output = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](activation, inputs, probs)
+        else:
+            output = _reference(activation(inputs), probs)
+        variables = [value for value in (inputs, probs) if value.requires_grad]
+        return output, *torch.autograd.grad(output, variables, upstream)
+
+    for actual, expected in zip(evaluate(True), evaluate(False), strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("phase", ["forward", "backward"])
+def test_weighted_glu_promoted_intermediates_are_bounded(
+    implementation: dict[str, Any], phase: str
+) -> None:
+    inputs = torch.randn(31, 14, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(31, 1, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+    products = _LargeFloatIntermediates()
+    if phase == "forward":
+        with products:
+            output = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+    else:
+        output = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+        with products:
+            torch.autograd.grad(output, (inputs, probs), torch.ones_like(output))
+    assert output.shape == (inputs.shape[0], inputs.shape[1] // 2)
+    assert 0 < products.largest <= implementation["_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS"]
+
+
+def test_weighted_glu_retains_only_input_storage(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """The activation graph must not retain additional full-size intermediates."""
+    inputs = torch.randn(31, 14, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(31, 1, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+
+    def retained_bytes(chunked: bool) -> int:
+        storages: dict[int, int] = {}
+
+        def pack(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            storage = tensor.untyped_storage()
+            storages[storage.data_ptr()] = storage.nbytes()
+            return tensor
+
+        with torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks(pack, lambda tensor: tensor):
+            if chunked:
+                output = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+            else:
+                output = _reference(_glu(inputs), probs)
+        # Keep the graph alive while measuring its saved tensors.
+        assert output.requires_grad
+        return sum(storages.values())
+
+    input_bytes = inputs.untyped_storage().nbytes() + probs.untyped_storage().nbytes()
+    assert retained_bytes(True) <= input_bytes
+    assert retained_bytes(False) > input_bytes
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("reentrant", [True, False])
+def test_weighted_glu_checkpoint_matches(implementation: dict[str, Any], reentrant: bool) -> None:
+    from torch.utils.checkpoint import checkpoint
+
+    values = torch.randn(13, 14, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = torch.rand(13, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+
+    def evaluate(chunked: bool) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:
+        inputs = values.clone().requires_grad_()
+        probs = weights.clone().requires_grad_()
+
+        def layer(inputs: torch.Tensor, probs: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+            if chunked:
+                return implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+            return _reference(_glu(inputs), probs)
+
+        output = checkpoint(layer, inputs, probs, use_reentrant=reentrant)
+        output.sum().backward()
+        assert inputs.grad is not None
+        assert probs.grad is not None
+        return output, inputs.grad, probs.grad
+
+    for actual, expected in zip(evaluate(True), evaluate(False), strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [0, 1, 2, 3, 13])
+def test_weighted_glu_boundary_sizes(implementation: dict[str, Any], rows: int) -> None:
+    inputs = torch.randn(rows, 14, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
+    probs = torch.rand(rows, 1, dtype=torch.float32, requires_grad=True)
+    actual = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+    expected = _reference(_glu(inputs), probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+    actual_grads = torch.autograd.grad(actual, (inputs, probs), torch.ones_like(actual))
+    expected_grads = torch.autograd.grad(expected, (inputs, probs), torch.ones_like(expected))
+    for actual_grad, expected_grad in zip(actual_grads, expected_grads, strict=True):
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual_grad, expected_grad, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_weighted_glu_noncontiguous_inputs_without_grad(implementation: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    inputs = torch.randn(14, 13, dtype=torch.bfloat16).t()
+    probs = torch.rand(13, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
+    with torch.no_grad():
+        actual = implementation["apply_weighted_activation"](_glu, inputs, probs)
+        expected = _reference(_glu(inputs), probs)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve autocast during activation recomputation**

When `enable_autocast=True` and a large gated activation uses an op whose CUDA autocast policy changes precision, the forward callback runs inside the autocast scope established in `megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/schedules.py:510-516`, but backward normally runs after that scope has exited and this recomputation restores only grad mode. For example, gated `squared_relu` runs its `torch.pow` in FP32 during the forward but recomputes it from the saved BF16 input here, so the FC1 and router gradients correspond to a different activation (and may also encounter a grad-output dtype mismatch). Preserve the forward autocast enabled state and dtype around the recomputation, such as by pairing AMP `custom_fwd`/`custom_bwd` decorators.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

+"""Bound mixed-precision router weighting in the forward and backward passes."""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import torch
+from torch.autograd.function import once_differentiable
+
+_MAX_TEMP_ELEMENTS = 16 * 1024 * 1024
+
+
+class _ChunkedRouterWeight(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Multiply router probabilities without retaining a full promoted product."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, activations, probs, chunk_rows):
+        """Apply the original promoted product to bounded row chunks."""
+        ctx.save_for_backward(activations if ctx.needs_input_grad[1] else None, probs)
+        ctx.activation_dtype = activations.dtype
+        ctx.chunk_rows = chunk_rows
+        ctx.product_dtype = torch.promote_types(activations.dtype, probs.dtype)
+        output = torch.empty_like(activations)
+        for start in range(0, activations.shape[0], chunk_rows):
+            end = start + chunk_rows
+            output[start:end].copy_(
+                (activations[start:end] * probs[start:end]).to(activations.dtype)
+            )
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        """Return activation and router gradients without a full promoted product."""
+        activations, probs = ctx.saved_tensors
+        grad_activations = torch.empty_like(grad_output) if ctx.needs_input_grad[0] else None
+        grad_probs = torch.empty_like(probs) if ctx.needs_input_grad[1] else None
+        for start in range(0, grad_output.shape[0], ctx.chunk_rows):
+            end = start + ctx.chunk_rows
+            # Match the gradient of the cast after the original promoted product.
+            grad = grad_output[start:end].to(ctx.product_dtype)
+            if grad_activations is not None:
+                grad_activations[start:end].copy_(
+                    (grad * probs[start:end]).to(ctx.activation_dtype)
+                )
+            if grad_probs is not None:
+                grad_probs[start:end].copy_(
+                    (grad * activations[start:end]).sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True).to(probs.dtype)
+                )
+        return grad_activations, grad_probs, None
+
+
+class _ChunkedWeightedActivation(torch.autograd.Function):
+    """Recompute a pointwise activation one row chunk at a time during backward."""
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, activation_func, inputs, probs, chunk_rows):
+        """Save inputs instead of retaining full eager activation intermediates."""
+        ctx.save_for_backward(inputs, probs)
+        ctx.activation_func = activation_func
+        ctx.chunk_rows = chunk_rows
+        output = None
+        for start in range(0, inputs.shape[0], chunk_rows):
+            end = start + chunk_rows
+            activation = activation_func(inputs[start:end])
+            if output is None:
+                output = activation.new_empty((inputs.shape[0], activation.shape[1]))
+            output[start:end].copy_((activation * probs[start:end]).to(activation.dtype))
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    @once_differentiable
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        """Recompute each activation chunk with its original autograd operations."""
+        inputs, probs = ctx.saved_tensors
+        needs_input, needs_probs = ctx.needs_input_grad[1:3]
+        grad_inputs = torch.empty_like(inputs) if needs_input else None
+        grad_probs = torch.empty_like(probs) if needs_probs else None
+        for start in range(0, inputs.shape[0], ctx.chunk_rows):
+            end = start + ctx.chunk_rows
+            with torch.enable_grad():
+                local_input = inputs[start:end].detach().requires_grad_(needs_input)
+                local_probs = probs[start:end].detach().requires_grad_(needs_probs)
+                activation = ctx.activation_func(local_input)
